request.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / animation cel drawing. Draw ONE complete 12-frame DISSOLUTION / OUTWARD RELEASE sprite sheet, 2048 x 1536 RGBA: exactly 4 columns by 3 rows of 512 x 512 cells, row-major time order. No gutters, labels, text, grid lines or borders. True transparent background. Every cell has center (256,256), the same fixed orthographic top-down view and the same pixel scale. Never recenter or auto-fit individual cels. Keep all remaining painted fragments within radius 244 and at least 12 pixels away from cell edges.

Reference image 1 is the EXACT initial mature pose registered at 512x512, outer radius about 220 pixels. Reference image 2 shows the larger approved identities. Begin at this pose, preserving its forty cyan/gold strips, varied notches/hooks/forks, nearby broken peripheral lanes and staggered gaps, large empty center. No purple, crystals, runes, diamonds or new decorative sparks.

CRITICAL: release is INDIVIDUALLY DRAWN FLUID MOTION AND DISINTEGRATION, not whole-image enlargement, not translating an intact finished circle and not uniformly lowering opacity. Track each strip continuously. Its head creeps outward and curls slightly, shoulder thins, tail is pulled into a narrow bent thread, a slit opens in the painted body, and the slit widens into separated curved shreds. These tiny shreds continue their own outward curling movement, shorten and taper to nothing. A given hook, fork and painted highlight must visibly change shape across adjacent cels. Use staggered local timing so strips do not all crack or vanish in one synchronized beat. Keep original angular order and color until each strip disappears. Do not grow whole large blades or invent unrelated particles.

Cel 0: exact supplied mature pose.
Cel 1: first individually redrawn tension; several long tails bow, short hooks open, no abrupt arrangement change.
Cel 2: different heads move a few pixels outward, thin shoulders and stretching tail tips; tiny interior slits begin.
Cel 3: drawn slits lengthen, tail forks curl differently; some long thin sections break into two clearly separated curved pieces.
Cel 4: more strips develop gaps along their length, colored shoulders thin; fragments drift into the near exterior, not into the empty center.
Cel 5: roughly half the painted mass remains as curled ribbons and short crescents; original broad silhouettes are no longer intact.
Cel 6: narrow separated shreds, hollow curves and short bent strokes; each continues a small outward motion.
Cel 7: only thin hooked slivers and tiny curved tails; several original strips have fully disappeared while others finish unfurling.
Cel 8: very sparse short curling remnants, with transparent gaps expanding between their newly drawn tapered ends.
Cel 9: only a handful of fine cyan and gold curved threads, no intact main arcs.
Cel 10: last few minute tapered traces close to the outer extent.
Cel 11: absolutely empty transparent cell.

The overall rotation will already have reached its runtime angle before release, so do not rotate the whole arrangement between these cells. Individual local curling and outward drift are visible and independent. Do not draw an enlarged completed ring at any point. All different strips and all broken-off pieces must remain separated by transparent air: NO touching, intersections, overlaps, occlusion or merging. Breaks are true transparent gaps in the drawing, not black outlines painted across an otherwise intact shape. No opaque disk, glow, fog, broad blur, background, floor, furnace or characters. Preserve Don't Starve Together crisp tapered hand-ink and simple cyan/gold painted material.
